tagline: A remote Western Desert oasis of mudbrick ruins, salt lakes, and the ancient Oracle of Amun that Alexander the Great once consulted

taxi.fareNote: Most sightseeing is arranged as a half or full-day tour with a local driver

emergency.note: Tourist police can assist; English support is limited this far from major resorts

visit: Shali Fortress mudbrick ruins
Temple of the Oracle of Amun
Gebel al Mawta rock-cut tombs
Cleopatra's Bath natural spring
the Great Sand Sea dune excursion
sunset at Fatnas Island lagoon
Salt lake floating (similar to the Dead Sea)
traditional Siwan handicraft shopping (silver jewelry, baskets)
overnight desert camping under the stars
walk: The town center and Shali Fortress are walkable; the salt lakes, springs, and Great Sand Sea require a car or guided excursion

safety.safety: Generally calm and welcoming; check current travel advisories for this part of Egypt's Western Desert before visiting
safety.crime: Low crime; the main risks relate to desert travel and remoteness rather than crime

hood_landmark.Shali Town Center: The Shali Fortress ruins towering over the modern town
hood_landmark.Temple of the Oracle (Aghurmi): The Temple of the Oracle of Amun
hood_landmark.Great Sand Sea (day-trip base): The rolling dunes of the Great Sand Sea

hood_desc: The heart of modern Siwa beneath the crumbling mudbrick Shali Fortress, with most guesthouses, restaurants, and the market.
A short ride from town, home to the ancient oracle temple where Alexander the Great reportedly sought confirmation of his divinity.
A popular natural spring pool where locals and visitors swim, especially refreshing after a hot day of sightseeing.
A small lagoon islet connected by causeway, beloved for sunset views over the palm groves and salt lake.
The vast dune sea south of town, reached by 4x4 for sandboarding, dune-bashing, and overnight desert camps.

transit.sys: Local taxis and guide-arranged 4x4 vehicles; no formal bus network within Siwa
transit.pay: Cash to the driver or guide
transit.map: Not centrally published; guesthouses arrange transport
transit.note: Bicycles are a popular and pleasant way to get around central Siwa itself

transport.air: No airport in Siwa; Marsa Matruh Airport is the nearest, about 3 hr away by road
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect Siwa to Alexandria and Cairo (8-11 hr journey)
transport.car: The Marsa Matruh-Siwa road is the main route in; a guide is recommended for any off-road desert travel

net.m: Limited 3G/4G in town, no coverage in the desert
net.w: Wifi available in some guesthouses but often slow
net.ops: Vodafone Egypt, Orange Egypt, Etisalat Misr
net.fwn: Wifi available in central guesthouses, though unreliable
net.ap: A Vodafone or Orange Egypt tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is customary and appreciated for desert guides
tip.r: Rounding up or 5-10% is appreciated, not obligatory

tagline: Bangladesh's 'tea capital,' a rolling patchwork of tea gardens, pineapple groves, and rainforest reserves
card: Rarely accepted; cash is essential throughout

taxi.fareNote: CNG auto-rickshaws are the standard way to reach tea gardens and Lawachara National Park

emergency.note: 999 connects to police, fire, and ambulance across Bangladesh

religion: Christianity (small minority, notably among tea-garden communities)
visit: Sreemangal's rolling tea gardens (Finlay, Deundi, and others)
the Nilkantha 'seven-layer tea' stall
Sreemangal town's local market
Lawachara National Park rainforest and gibbon-spotting trek
Madhabpur Lake (seasonal, for waterlilies)
Baikka Beel wetland bird sanctuary
Khasia betel-leaf village visit
pineapple and lemon orchard tours (seasonal)
tea factory tour and tasting
walk: Central Sreemangal town is walkable; the tea gardens, Lawachara National Park, and outlying villages require a CNG auto-rickshaw or car

safety.safety: Very safe, welcoming rural area popular with domestic tourists
safety.crime: Very low crime; standard rural-travel common sense applies

hood_landmark.Sreemangal Town Center: Sreemangal's tea-stall row and central market
hood_landmark.Tea Garden Belt: The rolling Finlay and Deundi tea estates
hood_landmark.Lawachara National Park: Lawachara's rainforest canopy and hoolock gibbons
hood_landmark.Madhabpur Lake Area: Madhabpur Lake's seasonal red and pink waterlilies
hood_landmark.Khasia Punji (Betel-leaf Villages): The indigenous Khasia community's betel-leaf plantations

hood_desc: The small commercial hub with the famous seven-layer tea stalls, guesthouses, and the local market; the practical base for exploring the region.
Endless rolling hills of manicured tea bushes surrounding town, best explored by bicycle or rickshaw at sunrise or sunset.
A protected rainforest reserve a short drive from town, home to Bangladesh's rare hoolock gibbons and forest trekking trails.
A seasonal lake known for its carpet of red and pink waterlilies, best visited in the winter dry season.
Indigenous Khasia communities cultivating betel-leaf gardens in the hills, offering a glimpse of local minority culture.

transit.map: Not centrally published; hotels arrange transport to tea gardens and the national park
transit.note: Hiring a CNG for a half or full day is the standard way to see the tea gardens and Lawachara

transport.air: Sylhet Osmani International Airport (ZYL), about 1.5-2 hr away, is the nearest airport
transport.train: Direct train service from Dhaka and Sylhet to Sreemangal station
transport.bus: Frequent long-distance buses connect to Dhaka (about 4-5 hr) and Sylhet
transport.car: Reachable via the Dhaka-Sylhet highway; hiring a car with driver from Dhaka is common

net.m: Moderate 3G/4G in town, patchier in the tea gardens and forest
net.ap: A Grameenphone or Robi prepaid SIM

tip.s: Not customary but appreciated for guides, roughly 5-10%
tip.r: Not expected; rounding up is a nice gesture

tagline: Bangladesh's only coral island, a tiny Bay of Bengal outpost of coconut palms and reef-fringed beaches
rides: Walking, bicycle, or auto-rickshaw (the island is small)

taxi.fare: Negotiated flat rate for the short trips available
taxi.fareNote: The island is small enough to explore mostly on foot or by rented bicycle

emergency.note: Medical facilities on the island are very basic; serious emergencies require evacuation to the mainland

visit: Snorkeling over the island's coral reef
walking the island's coconut-palm-lined coastline
sunset at the island's western beach
Boat trip to Chera Dwip (the islet separated at high tide)
local fishing village visit
fresh seafood at beachfront shacks
Cycling the island's single ring road
birdwatching (a stop for migratory species)
stargazing away from mainland light pollution
walk: The island is small enough to walk or cycle end to end in a couple of hours; there is no public transit

safety.safety: Generally safe, though facilities are basic and the island is remote; landing can be affected by monsoon-season sea conditions
safety.crime: Very low crime; the main risks are limited medical infrastructure and rough seas during the rainy season

hood_landmark.Main Village (Jetty Area): The island's jetty and main fishing village
hood_landmark.West Beach: The island's popular sunset-facing west beach
hood_landmark.Coral Reef Zone: The snorkeling reef fringing the island's south
hood_landmark.Chera Dwip (Golachipa): Chera Dwip, the islet cut off at high tide
hood_landmark.Northern Coconut Groves: The island's quiet northern coconut palm groves

hood_desc: The small settlement around the boat jetty, with most guesthouses, seafood shacks, and the local market.
A palm-lined stretch of beach on the island's west side, the best spot to watch the sunset over the Bay of Bengal.
The shallow reef surrounding the island, Bangladesh's only coral formation, best explored by snorkel at low tide.
A scenic islet reachable by boat or, at low tide, on foot, known for its dramatic isolation and quiet beaches.
A peaceful stretch of coconut groves on the island's quieter northern end, good for an escape from the jetty-area bustle.
lodging: Sea Pearl Beach Resort (mainland Cox's Bazar alternative)
Basic island lodging near the tip

transit.sys: No formal transit; the island is explored on foot or by rented bicycle
transit.map: Not applicable given the island's small size
transit.note: The island is reached only by boat from Teknaf, and access can be restricted or suspended during the June-September monsoon season

transport.air: Cox's Bazar Airport (CXB), then a road and boat journey to the island
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Cox's Bazar or Teknaf
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect Dhaka and Chittagong to Teknaf (about 10-12 hr from Dhaka)
transport.ferry: Passenger boats and speedboats run from Teknaf to Saint Martin's Island (seasonal, weather-dependent)
transport.car: A car or bus reaches Teknaf; the final leg to the island is by boat only

airport.name: Cox's Bazar Airport (nearest gateway)
airport.distance: ~110 km (road) plus boat crossing from Teknaf
airport.transport: Bus or car to Teknaf, then boat to the island

net.m: Limited 3G/4G coverage, unreliable in parts of the island
net.w: Wifi available in a few resorts but limited
net.gb: ~$3-8 for a prepaid tourist SIM (best purchased on the mainland)
net.fwn: Wifi limited to a handful of resorts
net.ap: A Grameenphone or Robi prepaid SIM, purchased before crossing to the island

tip.s: Not customary but appreciated for boat operators and guides
tip.r: Not expected; rounding up is a nice gesture

tagline: A misty highland town of terraced rice paddies and Hmong/Dao hill-tribe villages beneath Vietnam's highest peak
langs: Hmong, Dao, Tay, Giay (local minority languages)
card: Accepted at larger hotels; cash preferred at markets and small guesthouses

taxi.fareNote: Grab is reliable in town; motorbike taxis (xe om) are common for short hops

emergency.note: 113 for police, 115 for medical emergencies; English support is limited outside major hospitals

religion: animist/ancestor-worship traditions among Hmong and Dao communities
visit: Fansipan cable car to Vietnam's highest peak
Sa Pa's central lake and Stone Church
Muong Hoa Valley rice terrace viewpoints
Trekking to Cat Cat, Ta Van, or Lao Chai hill-tribe villages
Silver Waterfall and Love Waterfall
Bac Ha or Sa Pa Sunday/Saturday market
Multi-day homestay trek through the valley
Heaven's Gate mountain pass viewpoint
Ham Rong Mountain flower gardens
walk: Central Sa Pa town is walkable, though hilly; the terraced valleys and hill-tribe villages require a trek, motorbike, or car

safety.safety: Very safe town, popular with trekkers of all experience levels
safety.crime: Petty theft and pushy souvenir sellers in the market are the main concerns; trekking safety (weather, trail conditions) matters more

hood_landmark.Sa Pa Town Center: Sa Pa Lake and the Stone Church
hood_landmark.Cat Cat Village: Cat Cat Village's waterfall and Hmong stilt houses
hood_landmark.Ta Van / Lao Chai: Ta Van and Lao Chai's rice terrace trekking routes
hood_landmark.Fansipan Base (Cable Car): The Fansipan cable car base station
hood_landmark.Muong Hoa Valley: The Muong Hoa Valley's ancient rock carvings and terraces

hood_desc: The compact hill-station center around the lake and church, with most hotels, restaurants, and the tourist market.
A Hmong village a short walk from town, popular for an easy first trek through terraced fields to a waterfall.
Villages deeper in the valley reached by a half-day trek, offering homestays and closer contact with Hmong and Giay communities.
The base station for the cable car up Fansipan, Vietnam's highest peak, a short drive from the town center.
The broader valley of rice terraces and ancient stone carvings, the setting for Sa Pa's most scenic multi-day treks.

transit.sys: Local taxis, Grab, and motorbike rentals; trekking on foot is the norm for the valley
transit.map: Not centrally published; hotels and trekking agencies arrange guided routes
transit.note: Hiring a local guide (often from a Hmong or Dao village) is customary and directly supports the community

transport.air: No airport in Sa Pa; Noi Bai International Airport (HAN) in Hanoi is the main gateway
transport.train: Overnight train from Hanoi to Lao Cai, then a 1 hr transfer to Sa Pa
transport.bus: Direct sleeper buses connect Hanoi to Sa Pa (about 5-6 hr)
transport.car: A new expressway has cut the Hanoi-Sa Pa drive to around 5 hr

airport.name: Noi Bai International Airport, Hanoi (main gateway)
airport.transport: Sleeper bus, train via Lao Cai plus transfer, or private car

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier in the valley and villages
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in town
net.ap: A Viettel or Vinaphone tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is appreciated for trekking guides, especially on multi-day homestay treks
tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated

tagline: Vietnam's largest island, ringed by white-sand beaches, fish-sauce villages, and the world's longest sea cable car
card: Widely accepted at resorts; cash preferred at markets and small local eateries

taxi.fareNote: Grab is widely used and reliable across the island

emergency.note: 113 for police, 115 for medical emergencies; resort areas have some English support

visit: Bai Sao (Sao Beach) white sand and turquoise water
Hon Thom cable car (the world's longest over-sea cable car)
Duong Dong night market
Phu Quoc Prison historical site
fish sauce (nuoc mam) factory tour
Sunset Sanato Beach Club at Long Beach
VinWonders and Vinpearl Safari theme parks
snorkeling/diving trip to the An Thoi archipelago
Suoi Tranh waterfall
walk: Duong Dong town is walkable for its market and waterfront; the island's beaches and attractions are spread out and best reached by scooter, taxi, or Grab

safety.safety: Very safe island, popular with families and honeymooners
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded beaches is the main concern

hood_landmark.Duong Dong (Town Center): Duong Dong Night Market and Dinh Cau Rock Temple
hood_landmark.An Thoi (South): An Thoi's harbor and cable car terminal
hood_landmark.Bai Sao (Sao Beach): Bai Sao's white sand and turquoise shallows
hood_landmark.Ganh Dau (North): Ganh Dau's quieter northern beaches and forest

hood_desc: The island's main town, with the night market, fishing harbor, and most everyday services; a lively, less resort-y base.
The island's famous sunset-facing beach strip, lined with resorts, beach clubs, and restaurants.
The southern port town and departure point for the Hon Thom cable car and boat trips to the An Thoi archipelago.
One of the island's most photographed beaches, with powder-white sand and shallow turquoise water.
A quieter, less developed northern area with forest, small beaches, and views toward Cambodia.
lodging: JW Marriott Phu Quoc Emerald Bay

transit.sys: Grab and local taxis; scooter rental is very popular
transit.map: Not centrally published; scooter rental is the most flexible way to explore
transit.note: Renting a scooter is common for visitors comfortable riding; otherwise Grab covers the island well

transport.air: Phu Quoc International Airport (PQC), with direct domestic and some international flights
transport.bus: Local buses connect the airport, Duong Dong, and Long Beach
transport.ferry: High-speed ferries connect to Ha Tien and Rach Gia on the Vietnamese mainland
transport.car: Rental cars and scooters are available; roads circle most of the island

net.m: Good 4G coverage across most of the island
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Viettel or Vinaphone tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for tour guides

tagline: A UNESCO-listed lantern-lit trading port frozen in time, where tailor shops and river cruises meet a nearby beach
card: Accepted at larger hotels and restaurants; cash preferred in the Ancient Town's shops and markets

taxi.fareNote: Grab is reliable; renting a bicycle is a popular way to reach An Bang Beach

emergency.note: 113 for police, 115 for medical emergencies; English support is decent given heavy tourism

religion: ancestor worship and folk traditions widely practiced alongside
visit: Hoi An Ancient Town's lantern-lit streets and Japanese Covered Bridge
the Chinese assembly halls (Fujian, Cantonese)
Hoi An Central Market
Custom tailoring at the Ancient Town's tailor shops
An Bang Beach for swimming and beach bars
riverside lantern boat ride at night
Cooking class or basket-boat ride in the coconut palm forest (Cam Thanh)
cycling through rural rice paddies
day trip to My Son Sanctuary Cham ruins
walk: The Ancient Town is a pedestrian-friendly UNESCO site, best explored entirely on foot; An Bang Beach is a short bicycle or Grab ride away

safety.safety: Very safe town, popular with travelers of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft and overcharging by unlicensed vendors in the Ancient Town are the main concerns

hood_landmark.Ancient Town (Old Quarter): The Japanese Covered Bridge and lantern-lit riverside streets
hood_landmark.An Bang Beach: An Bang Beach's row of beach bars and loungers
hood_landmark.Cam Thanh (Coconut Village): Cam Thanh's coconut palm forest and basket-boat rides
hood_landmark.Cam Nam Island: Cam Nam Island's quiet riverside cafes across the bridge
hood_landmark.New Town (Tan An): The newer commercial district beyond the Ancient Town

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed heart of Hoi An, a car-free maze of lantern-strung streets, tailor shops, and centuries-old merchant houses; the essential base for any visit.
A relaxed beach a short bike ride from the Ancient Town, popular for sunset drinks and swimming.
A rural riverside village known for its round basket-boat rides through coconut palm channels, just outside town.
A quiet island across a small bridge from the Ancient Town, with a more local, low-key riverside feel.
The modern part of Hoi An beyond the historic core, with everyday shops and more affordable local dining.
lodging: La Siesta Hoi An Beach Resort

transit.sys: Bicycle rental (very popular), Grab, and local taxis
transit.hours: Roughly 6am-10pm for Grab; the Ancient Town restricts vehicle traffic in the evening
transit.map: Not centrally published; bicycle rental shops are everywhere
transit.note: Motorbikes and cars are restricted within the Ancient Town during certain hours; walking and cycling are the norm

transport.air: Da Nang International Airport (DAD), about 30-40 min away
transport.train: Da Nang railway station connects to the national rail network; a taxi/Grab covers the final leg to Hoi An
transport.bus: Local buses and shuttle services connect Da Nang and Hoi An
transport.car: Well connected via Highway 1 and the coastal road from Da Nang

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Viettel or Vinaphone tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for tour guides and tailors

tagline: An ancient cave-dwelling city carved into limestone ravines, among the oldest continuously inhabited settlements on Earth
card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small cave-district shops

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.50 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; the Sassi districts are pedestrian-only in many areas

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

visit: Sasso Caveoso and Sasso Barisano cave districts
Matera Cathedral
rock-cut churches (San Pietro Caveoso, Madonna delle Virtù)
Casa Grotta cave-house museums
Palombaro Lungo underground cistern
MUSMA contemporary sculpture museum in a cave palazzo
Murgia Materana Park hike across the ravine for the classic Sassi panorama
day trip to nearby Puglia trulli towns
sunset/night illumination viewpoint from Belvedere Luigi Guerricchio
walk: The Sassi districts are compact but very hilly and stepped, best explored slowly on foot; comfortable shoes are essential

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular with visitors of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; the main practical caution is uneven, steep stone paths at night

hood_landmark.Sasso Caveoso: San Pietro Caveoso church overlooking the ravine
hood_landmark.Sasso Barisano: The rock-cut churches and cave hotels of Sasso Barisano
hood_landmark.Civita: Matera Cathedral atop the Civita ridge
hood_landmark.Piano (Modern Town): Piazza Vittorio Veneto and the Palombaro Lungo cistern
hood_landmark.Murgia Materana Park (across the ravine): The Belvedere panorama across the Gravina ravine

hood_desc: The older, more atmospheric of the two cave districts, with rock-cut churches and sweeping ravine views; ideal for boutique cave-hotel stays.
The larger, more developed cave district with the highest concentration of cave hotels, restaurants, and shops.
The elevated ridge between the two Sassi, crowned by the Romanesque cathedral with panoramic views over both districts.
The modern city center beyond the Sassi, with everyday shops, the main square, and the underground cistern museum.
A nature park across the ravine offering the classic postcard view back at the cave city, plus ancient rock churches and hiking trails.

transit.sys: Ferrovie Appulo Lucane (FAL) local rail and Matera urban bus network
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; tickets also sold at kiosks
transit.note: The Sassi districts are pedestrian-only in many areas; a car is unnecessary within the historic center

transport.air: Bari Karol Wojtyla Airport (BRI), about 1 hr away, is the main regional gateway
transport.train: FAL local rail connects Matera to Bari (about 1.5 hr)
transport.bus: Regional buses (Marino, Miccolis) connect to Bari, Naples, and Rome
transport.car: Well connected via the SS7 and SS99 roads; parking is available near the modern town, with the Sassi being car-free

airport.name: Bari Karol Wojtyla Airport
airport.transport: FAL train, shuttle bus, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is common instead of tipping; rounding up is a nice gesture

tagline: Five pastel-colored fishing villages clinging to Italy's Ligurian coast, linked by cliffside hiking trails
card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small village shops and trail huts
rides: Regional train between villages (the primary way to get around)
local boats between villages in season

taxi.fare: Metered where available; limited taxi service given the villages' small size
taxi.fareNote: The Cinque Terre train and coastal boats are far more practical than taxis for getting between villages

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

visit: Sentiero Azzurro (Blue Trail) hiking between villages
Manarola's harbor at sunset
Vernazza's Doria Castle and harbor
Monterosso al Mare's beach (the largest in Cinque Terre)
Riomaggiore's colorful cliffside houses
Corniglia's terraced vineyard views (the only village not on the sea)
Cinque Terre National Park Card for trail and transit access
boat tour along the coastline
local pesto and Sciacchetrà wine tasting
walk: Each village is small and walkable, though very hilly with many stairs; moving between villages is by train, boat, or the famous (sometimes closed for landslide repair) coastal trails

safety.safety: Very safe, though trails can be strenuous and occasionally close due to landslides or bad weather
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded trains and trails in peak season is the main concern

hood_landmark.Monterosso al Mare: Monterosso's Fegina beach, the largest in Cinque Terre
hood_landmark.Riomaggiore: Riomaggiore's colorful stacked houses and the Via dell'Amore trailhead

Widely considered the most picturesque village, with a small natural harbor, colorful houses, and a hilltop castle.
The only village not directly on the sea, perched on a hilltop amid vineyards and reached by a long staircase or shuttle bus.
Famous for its postcard view of pastel houses stacked above a tiny harbor, especially photogenic at sunset.
The southernmost village, with dramatic cliffside houses and the start of the Via dell'Amore coastal path to Manarola.

transit.pay: Cinque Terre Card (includes train and trail access) or individual tickets
transit.note: The train is by far the easiest way between villages; cars are discouraged and parking is very limited

transport.bus: Limited local shuttle buses connect Corniglia's station to the hilltop village

net.m: Good 4G coverage in villages, patchier on the coastal trails
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels

Marina Grande beach and the town's central steps
MAR Roman Archaeological Museum
Fornillo Beach for a quieter alternative to Marina Grande
Path of the Gods (Sentiero degli Dei) clifftop hike (starting nearby)
boat trip to Li Galli islets or Capri
Day trip along the Amalfi Coast to Amalfi and Ravello
limoncello tasting
sunset aperitivo on a terrace overlooking the harbor

hood_landmark.Marina Grande: Marina Grande beach and Santa Maria Assunta's majolica dome
hood_landmark.Montepertuso: Montepertuso's hilltop village and natural rock arch

hood_landmark.Via Cristoforo Colombo (Upper Town): The upper town's boutique-lined main road

A hilltop village above Positano reached by local bus, with sweeping views and a famous natural rock arch.
An even higher, quieter hamlet at the trailhead for the Path of the Gods hike, offering dramatic coastal panoramas.
The steep main street winding down from the top of town, lined with boutiques, ceramics shops, and cafes.

transport.bus: SITA buses connect Positano to Sorrento, Amalfi, and Salerno along the coast road
